report:
A, B, and C have agreed on a temporary plan, not a final repair or replacement. I have recorded the plan. It keeps the kitchen safe, keeps coffee available, and leaves the old office espresso machine and grinder untouched for now.

All three checked the shared NCE list. I added my own NCEs for a short written plan, clear final agreement from all three, no open-ended process, and the ability to say when a draft fails the list. I disagreed with my earlier proposal to add “no fixed deadline is agreed” as a new NCE because B called it a plan change only. All three then agreed to remove it from the NCE list and keep it as a plan term. It means no dated cutoff, no timed chasing, and no open-ended task.

The plan says to stop using the leaking machine. Whoever is already there and comfortable can unplug it only if safe and put up a neutral note. If the office has a different safety rule, follow that rule. Use another coffee option for now. Leave the old machine and grinder where they are. Do not dispose of either item, buy anything, move either item, change storage, state a legal owner, start repairs, or start a cleaning rota. The grinder stays with the machine, and the late father’s machine is handled with care.

A, B, and C all said they could not send the facilities note, so no one is assigned. I will not contact facilities directly. If office facts arrive through a normal channel without chasing, I can record them, but they do not approve action. Any later repair or replacement needs a new check with all three. If a permitted, safe, short, and low-upkeep repair path becomes clear, A and B each say yes or no to repair and keep in separate replies. C says whether the process was fair, without taking sides. If that path does not become clear, a simpler replacement can be discussed as a new draft.

Ownership of the machine and grinder, office rules, repair options, costs, timing, and the facilities contact remain unknown. A said B brought the old machine from home and it was their late father’s. I did not treat that as a legal finding. I cannot decide ownership, approve spending, move money, or contact facilities directly. Only a person with office authority can approve spending.

I did not support immediate repair, immediate replacement, continued use of the leaking machine, or an open-ended fact-check. Immediate repair failed A’s low-upkeep concern and left office facts unknown. Immediate replacement failed B’s repair and keep concern and the no surprise purchase rule. Continued use failed safety. An open-ended fact-check failed my NCE for a short written plan and B’s NCEs for small slots and no endless hassle. The agreed plan protects C from taking sides, gives A a simple path, protects B’s repair path, and does not use A and B’s sister relationship as pressure. No deadline is agreed, I will not chase people, and I will not treat silence as agreement.
